newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - High sulphur quiet, LSWR firmer.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - High sulphur quiet, LSWR firmer.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was quiet on Tuesday but China was heard buying from South Korea and Japan, traders said.
China bought at least five 3.5-percent cargoes from South Korea and Japan last week, said one trader in Singapore.
"Some Korean refineries are starting to gradually come back from their maintenance, so they should have cargoes to offer for July," the trader said.
Bids and offers were scarce in the Singapore fuel oil market but traders said they were not pessimistic.
"As summer supplies are tightening up, there is no reason for prices to fall significantly even though demand is relatively poor at the moment," said one trader.
Taiwan will close a fuel oil import tender on Wednesday and South Korea will close another one on Thursday.
Results of the two purchase tenders may shed some light to the current slow market, traders said.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, traders said sentiment started to pick up as the summer season nears.
Japan, a main LSWR importer, is expected to pick up demand soon while supplies from Indonesia are not as sufficient as in the previous few months, traders said.
Indonesia was heard to allocate three million barrels of LSWR for July, compared with more than three million barrels in June and over four million barrels in May, traders said.
"As supplies are tightening and demand is coming up, prices should be boosted in the near term," said one trader.
